I think this game could be so much better if people competent in tennis would have been involved in the design.

The Pros:
1) it's a VR tennis game!
2) teleport movement it's a smart way to move around the court in VR

The negative
1) physics are still very very bad, even after the latest update. (producing a correct tennis swing doesn't produce a good shot, but flicking your wrists as you would do with the nintendo Wii does...)
3) once the physics would be decent, then the players should be able to choose their favorite grips for forehand, backhand, serve, etc..., and be able to switch between one or the other with a button or the joystick
4) the model of the racket is gross, choppy, unrealistic (same the grip)
5) once physics would make any sense, there should be different rackets types, with different meanings (control, power, spin) and different racket head sizes. Same should be done for the strings.
6) there should be a swing path analyzer that could tell you how much the path of your racket corresponds to the most common ideal paths of certain shots, and a VR tutor could actually show how the proper tennis movement should be done. in this way you could try to mimic it and confront your shots.
7) the animations and the graphic in general are very basic, considering that the whole level is just a tennis court and it's immediate surroundings, the graphic could look photorealistic without a big hit on performance
8) when hitting the ball, there should be a vibration feedback that corresponds to then stiffness of the racket and strings, the power of the shot and the type of shot.
9) a simulation mode should be introduced together with full body tracking (specifically feet, hips and shoulders), in order to have a realistic shot representation in VR

At the moment this is a very arcady game that I don't recommend.

This is an excellent tennis experience and is extremely fun to play. This isn't much of a game though, this is a simulator like the title says. If you've played real tennis, you'll probably like this game. This isn't Wii Sports tennis, this is simulating playing tennis. 

The game does have some quirks:

Small issue, the crowd. I love the crowd responses in the matches, but they only seem to cheer sometimes. There have been some matches where the crowd cheers after the first point, and then is silent for a whole game or two and then comes back out of nowhere. At first I thought it was funny like they stopped cheering if you were beating your opponent really badly, but I think it's just a bug. Maybe have a slider for how often the crowd responds.

Another small issue, free movement is very weird. Side to side is perfect and I have no issues with it, but when you move up and back on the court it seems to have some kind of odd acceleration/deceleration, especially moving backwards it feels like I'm fighting the player to move backwards.

My main issue with the game comes with the physics modes. Arcade is really fun, and is accurate and adjusts your shots just enough to make you a bit more consistent. Simulation mode is a really good simulation of tennis, but it has some issues.  The main issue I have with Simulation mode is that it's difficult to get the racket response exactly how you're used to it in real life. It's hard to perfectly align your hand and you can't roll the racket in your hand like you can in real life (I play on Index so I can't even roll the controller), so you have to use more wrist movement rather than adjusting your grip. I think the main problem with racket response is really the fact that there's no racket customization like you get in real life. In real life I play with decently tight strings, a vibration dampener and a bit of weighted tape at the tip of the head. You can't get that kind of detailed response in this game.

All that said, I have tons of fun playing this game. There's a wide variety of courts and surfaces for matches, the AI is very fun to play against and is decently challenging even on the easiest difficulty, and it can be a fun VR workout. 

Things I wish would be changed/added to the game:

Racket customization for simulation mode. A slider for tight/loose strings and vibration dampener on/off would be great but I don't think it's 100% necessary.

More practice court variety. There's only one practice court building and you can change the surface, but you're always in the same building. Maybe even simply indoor vs outdoor for some variety.

Add a practice partner mode to practice. Just an AI partner you can hit the ball back and forth with without having to play a match, maybe even a mini game to see how many hits back and forth you can get before one of you hits it out.

Some things that would be nice to have but really aren't necessary would be a full VR body so you can see your player's outfit outside of just the character creation screen, and of course racket smashing would be awesome but totally unnecessary. 

Overall, excellent game and I highly recommend it if you like tennis.

リアル寄りのVRテニスゲーム。必殺技とかなく、シンプルに打って返すテニス。

といってもそこはゲームなので、アーケードモードであれば実際のテニスよりはかなり簡単に玉を返せるようになっている。とりあえずラケットに玉が当たれば、よほどへんな打ち方をしない限り相手のコートに玉が返る。シミュレーションモードというのもあって、試してはないけどこちらはたぶん力加減なども加味されての返球になるっぽい。実際のテニスをほとんどやったことがないのでリアルとは比較できないが、打つ感覚に違和感は感じない。打ったと思って当たらない・・・なんてのはたぶんリアルでもあること。

ゲームは世界中を回ってトーナメントに参加して行くシナリオモード。最初にステータスの割り振りなどが軽くある。各地でトーナメントに参加して勝つとポイントがもらえて２回戦、準決勝、決勝と進む・・・らしい。まだ１回戦しか勝ったことがないけれど。
単発のエキジビションモードがないのがちょっと残念だが、練習モードに試合形式の練習はある。対人マッチも可能らしく、挑戦OKにしているとたまーに対戦申請がくる。へたっぴなので受けたことないけど。ただしプレイ人数は非常に少ないのであまり期待はできない。

練習モードもあって、ピッチングマシーン？から玉を飛ばしてくるものと、練習試合が選べる。ピッチングマシーンはフォア、バック、ミックスなど選択できるので、なれるまではこちらでやってみるのもよいかも。

最初はなかなかラケットに玉が当たらなかったけど、だいぶ返し方がわかってきた。それでもたまにスカってムカっとくるし、なかなか勝てないけど、ゲーム補正もあるのでやっていけばたまに勝ったりもできる。

気になる点も少し。これは回線やデバイスのせいもあるかもしれないが、たまにラグが生じる。特にここぞという場面でラグってミスるとヘコむ。そういうこともある、ということを念頭に置いて気軽に遊ぶ必要がある。

運動量的にはけっこうハード。２試合もすると汗だく。そんなに素早くラケットを振る必要はないが、それでもそこそこ腕に来る。そこそこ良い運動にはなると思う。ただし片腕しか使わないので、片腕だけ筋肉痛になったりする。

VRスペースについて。動きが大きくなるし、玉を追う必要もあるので、そこそこの広さが必要。壁をぶんなぐらないように注意。移動については、移動なし（リアルに移動）、自分で操作して移動、テレポートで自動移動、など選択できる。テレポートで移動が一番シンプルだし場所も取らないので遊びやすい。
ただしテレポートの場合、勝手にネット際に寄ることがあるのだが、これが非常に困る。まずネット際で打つのが難しい、さらに一度前に出ると後ろに戻ってくれないので、相手に返されるとほぼ手が出ない。この勝手にネット寄りが地味にイライラする。スティックボタンで任意にネット寄りができるのだから、勝手に寄るのはなしにして欲しい。この点だけ注意。

日本語も対応している。ただしアナウンスは英語。得点のコールと、実況中継があるが、へたっぴだと嫌味言われるので実況中継はオフにしている。

まだたまにしか勝てないが、それでもちょっとなれてくるとテニスしてる感を味わえるなかなか良いゲーム。

アーケードモードで試合に勝てるくらいになったので追記。

アーケードモードとシミュレーションモードという2つのゲームモードがあるが、アーケードモードはラケットに球が当たればほぼ確実に相手コートに球が返るお気軽モード。なんならラケットを振らなくても、球の軌跡にラケットがあるだけで返球できる。その場合左右にアウトすることはあっても、手前や奥に球でアウトになることはほぼない。最初は無理に振るより、ラケットを置くくらいの気持ちでやってみるのもよいかも。ただしラケットを振らないと球の速度が落ちる。ゆっくりな球を送ると、相手からの返球速度が速くなるし、コースの打ち分けも難しいのでので、慣れてきたらやはり多少でもラケットを振った方がいい。

どうしても球に当たらないという人は、とにかく球を見てみるとよいかも。まず右に来るか左に来るかを判断してそちらにラケットを構え、球の模様が見えるくらいじっくり見て、体の少し前くらいでラケットが当たるようにすると返せる・・・かも。そうやって球の模様が見えるくらいまでじっくり見えるというのもVRならでは。

一方シミュレーションモードは、ラケットの角度や振った強さによってリアルに返球される。ある程度勢いをつけて振らないと相手コートに返らないし、強すぎるとアウトになる。別ゲーと思うくらいにゲーム感覚が変わるので、リアル志向の方はこちらをどうぞ。

当たれば返る、はCPUにも言えることで、通常のポジションにいて返球がサイド以外でアウトになることはまずない。そのサイドアウトも数%程度。しかもCPUは、正面に来た球はほぼほぼ100%返してくる。そのため点を取るには、相手の届かないところに打ち込むか、サイドアウトになるまで粘ってラリーを続けるしかない。もう１つだけ、なぜかCPUはコードの前側にいるときの高い球に異常に弱い。高い球は普通ならスマッシュのチャンスだと思うのだけれど、一桁ランカーでも高いたかはスカってしまう。なので相手が前に出てきたら、ラケットを振り上げるように振って高い球を上げればだいたいポイントが取れる。

移動をワープモードにしていると、たまに勝手にコートの真ん中当たりやネット際に移動することがある。チャンスを与えてくれてるつもりかもしれないが、非常に返球がしづらく、どちらかというと罠か罰ゲームに感じる。ネット際になったら、相手の球を無理に打とうとせず、ラケットに当てて下に落とすだけにすると良い感じ。ネットに触れようが相手のコートに踏み込もうが反則は取られないのでご心配なく。コートの真ん中あたりになったときが曲者で、スマッシュは打ちづらいし、普通に返すと相手の返球に反応できないし、下手に狙うとすぐアウトになってしまうしで困る。一度前に出たら後ろには戻れないみたいなので、頑張って凌ぐしかない。

移動はワープモードしかしたことがないが、リアルモードというのもあって、実際に走って返球できるらしい。体育館や倉庫くらいの広いところでやったらどうなるんだろう、と思うけれどそんなところでVRができる環境はないので試すことはできないけれど。

I have really tried to like this game. I really have. I've played for approximately 20 hours and I just can't stand it anymore. I bought it because I read somewhere it's the best VR tennis game there is. I sincerely do hope that isn't the case.

Tl:dr: Don't buy it if you're looking for VR tennis. This game is so far removed from tennis due to its mechanics and its quirks and errors that you have to relearn everything you know to come anywhere close to being competent and I simply don't want to do that.

There are several key things wrong with the mechanics of the game, the most grueling two being the force calculation and the trajectory calculation after impact with the racket. When you hit the ball with the racket, the ball gets projected in the direction you hit it in [b] the millisecond it made contact with the racket, [/b], meaning anything else that happens after does not affect its trajectory. This is fine for shots where the ball hits the racket and rebounds quickly, but it's a garbage way to calculate smashes, for example. When you're at the net and you try to hit a smash, everything depends on how the racket hits the ball initially. It doesn't matter if you follow through by continuing to move the racket downward, the ball doesn't care. This means you can't hit a proper smash, because the ball will just limp forward in the direction your racket was pointed the instant you hit it and the smash becomes a drop shot and it ruins the rally. 

This is all for Arcade, by the way. It gets amplified in Simulation, where if you don't angle the racket just right, the ball will either fly way out or hit the net. Remember before when I said this calculation method mostly worked for forehands and backhands? Well, in Simulation, that is no longer the case. Because the game isn't forcing the ball to go in the right direction anymore, a simple backhand turns into a nightmare.

The force calculation is also done incorrectly. When you hit a ball, the game tries (tries) to calculate how fast the ball should rebound. I don't know how it does this for sure, but I do know that it leads to you ending up flicking your wrist more than properly swinging your arm, because the latter is useless. If a ball is approaching and you swing your arm as you normally would for a tennis game, (besides causing your headset to not be able to track your controller momentarily, glitching the game out, though this isn't a problem with the more expensive headsets with tracking towers which most people don't have) you hit the ball slower than you would if you just place the racket in front of the ball and flick your wrist forward. This, combined with the bad direction calculation, only exacerbates these problems.

Another huge problem the game has is the movement in general. As I've said, there are several ways you can move around the court, the main ones being the joystick and the auto run. Both are broken.

When you try to run with your joystick, for some reason, you barely move at all sometimes, rendering it useless, at least for me. There probably is some way for it to work or some specific thing I have to do with my hand to force it to work, but if you can't tell from this review, I am done learning this game's every error and its fix to just be able to play. I am therefore forced to use Auto run, which is probably the single most broken thing in the game. I've been thinking about writing a review on this game but I kept giving it chance after chance after chance, and I just played a match where the AI screwed me so many times I just decided it was time.

First off, the AI decides whether you're hitting a forehand or a backhand by either standing to the left or to the right of the ball, and generally, it does a good job of predicting what you want to do. But not that rarely, when you're running after the ball, as you approach it, it randomly decides to switch at the very last second, when you're already positioned to hit a forehand, for example, and the ball has already passed you before you can do anything. This has happened enough times to warrant a mention here. Sometimes, the AI also just decides to move forwards for absolutely no reason. The ball is coming in diagonally and you could hit it if you just move left a little, but the AI decides that it would be a better course of action to run up to the net for no reason, making hitting the ball literally impossible.

Yet another problem, which happens every single time someone hits a lob, is that the AI works in a way where it decides to go somewhere once the opponent has hit the ball, goes there and just stays there until you hit the ball again, which means that sometimes, when the opponent hits a lob or a drop shot and forces you to run up to the net, the AI calculates where it should place you, runs up and stops dead in its tracks, making hitting the shot impossible. I've hit the ceiling with my controller several times just from trying to jump high enough to hit a shot I could have hit by just moving backwards. Another case where this is a problem is when the ball bounces next to you. Instead of moving back, it just stays right where it is, forcing you to hit very low (and therefore very weak) shots to continue the rally. And when it isn't doing that, when you run up to hit a shot, instead of taking on more of an intermediate position, it runs all the way back to the center mark, and since when you return a far left shot in this game it almost always is another far left shot, you can't do anything and have to watch as the ball flies past you while the AI panics.

The final problem I have with the movement is that the game thinks you are in an actual tennis court, because it expects you to launch yourself horizontally Monfils-style sometimes. It just stops and expects YOU to move the remaining distance to hit the shot comfortably, which just doesn't work, and I have a fairly large play area. These five problems I have just listed have happened in about 50% of the rallies in a single 3 set match. Unplayable.

On top of all this, it's a buggy mess. It crashes about 10% of the times you try to boot it up, it occasionally locks up when you try to enter a game mode, select a language or enter a match forcing you to close it (and sometimes it locks up again after doing that), your racket disappears sometimes and you have to delete your entire character to fix it, your opponents may become invisible, the ball sometimes just flies out in a random direction when you hit it in the most slightly unorthodox way, the force calculation sometimes bugs out and doesn't give the ball enough force to even make it past the net (even after hitting it with the same exact way as a previous, successful shot), the ball sometimes disappears, softlocking the game and forcing you to restart the entire match and more things I can't remember right now.

They're good because they learned every single quirk and mastered every single technique associated with playing [b] this game. [/b] I want to play [b] tennis, [/b] and as I have explained in this review, this game isn't tennis. It's based on tennis, but the way the mechanics work forces you to completely relearn everything you know about playing real tennis, and this comes from someone who has played tennis for over 12 years.

I have tried to look past everything I have mentioned in this review, but today I reached my breaking point. If you are willing to spend hundreds of hours mastering this game's every quirk and mechanic, yes, you can get better and enjoy yourself. But I don't. I want to play [b] tennis.
